::: {#exm-best-discriminator}

#### Where the GAN's discriminator ended up

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
with torch.no_grad():
    d_real = torch.sigmoid(discriminator(standardized)).mean().item()
    made_up = generator_net(torch.randn(1000, 2, generator=draws))
    d_fake = torch.sigmoid(discriminator(made_up)).mean().item()
print(d_real, d_fake)
```

If the generator of @exm-gan matched the data exactly,
@thm-best-discriminator says the best discriminator would give $\frac{1}{2}$ to every point.
The trained discriminator gives the real eruptions an average probability of `r sprintf("%.2f", py$d_real)` of being real,
and the made-up ones `r sprintf("%.2f", py$d_fake)`.
The generator does not match the data,
as @fig-gan shows,
so this is not the best discriminator:
a small network, trained a step at a time against a moving generator,
has stopped telling the two apart on average,
though the theorem says a better one could.

:::
